svg.text: Figure 1a — Runtime Architecture and Threat Overview
Juice Shop · 20.1.1 · 7 components · 18 data flows · 4 trust boundaries · 52 threats in the model

g.title: Trust boundary crossing: tb-1 External → C-02; tb-2 External → C-03; tb-6 C-02 → External; tb-7 C-05 → External
df-001: User input; evidence: frontend/src/app/app.routing.ts:None, frontend/src/app/app.component.ts:None

df-002: POST /rest/user/login with email and password credentials (HTTPS) df-003: POST /rest/2fa/verify with TOTP code and temporary JWT token from login step 1 (HTTPS) df-002 authentication: public login endpoint; credentials submitted in request body; evidence: routes/login.ts:18 df-002 access group: Credentials (2FA if enrolled); sequence; step 1 df-003 authentication: tmpToken in request body (short-lived JWT issued at password verification, before full authentication); evidence: routes/2fa.ts:17 df-003 access group: Credentials (2FA if enrolled); sequence; step 2

df-004: POST /rest/user/login with credentials derived from Google access_token (btoa of reversed email) (HTTPS) df-004 authentication: password field set to btoa(email.split('').reverse().join('')) derived from Google access_token; inherently reversible encoding; evidence: frontend/src/app/oauth/oauth.component.ts:30
df-005: POST /rest/user/reset-password with security question answer (HTTPS)

df-006: Authenticated REST API requests with JWT Bearer token in Authorization header (HTTPS) df-006 authentication: RS256-signed JWT stored in localStorage, sent as Authorization: Bearer header; verified by lib/insecurity.ts express-jwt middleware; evidence: frontend/src/app/Services/request.interceptor.ts:16, lib/insecurity.ts:156 df-006 access group: REST API; alternatives; step n/a

df-007: Unauthenticated REST API requests to public endpoints (registration, product browsing, feedback) (HTTPS) df-007 authentication: publicly accessible routes with no authentication middleware; includes user registration and public product data; evidence: server.ts:402 df-007 access group: REST API; alternatives; step n/a

df-008: POST / data erasure request authenticated via session cookie (token field) (HTTPS) df-008 authentication: token cookie checked against authenticated user map in lib/insecurity.ts authenticatedUsers; evidence: routes/dataErasure.ts:76 df-008 access group: REST API; alternatives; step n/a

df-009: WebSocket connection and bidirectional Socket.IO events (challenge solved notifications, score updates) (WebSocket) df-009 authentication: No authentication check; confirmed by T-042 (evidence-verified); evidence: lib/startup/registerWebsocketEvents.ts:23

df-010: Sequelize ORM queries to SQLite (user, product, order, feedback, card, address records) (SQLite) df-010 authentication: Embedded SQLite engine inside the application process; the engine has no login of its own.; evidence: models/index.ts:34

df-011: MarsDB in-memory document operations for product reviews and orders collections (MarsDB) df-011 authentication: Embedded MarsDB engine inside the application process; the engine has no login of its own.; evidence: data/mongodb.ts:9, data/mongodb.ts:10

df-012: POST /rest/chat triggers streamed LLM inference request to Ollama-compatible HTTP endpoint (HTTP) df-012 authentication: Ollama endpoint URL from config; no API key or auth header found in routes/chat.ts chat() function; evidence: routes/chat.ts:114

df-015: WebSocket subscription to Ethereum Sepolia NFTMinted contract events via Alchemy RPC (WebSocket) df-015 authentication: Alchemy API key embedded in WebSocket URL via process.env.ALCHEMY_API_KEY; evidence: routes/nftMint.ts:18

df-016: POST /file-upload multipart form data with no authentication check (HTTPS) df-016 authentication: POST /file-upload has no authentication middleware; authn_signal: absent confirmed in route inventory; evidence: routes/fileUpload.ts:19 df-016 access group: REST API; alternatives; step n/a
df-018: User input; evidence: frontend/src/app/app.guard.ts:48, frontend/src/app/app.routing.ts:81, frontend/src/hacking-instructor/challenges/adminSection.ts:72
Internet Attacker → C-03 · Authentication and Session Service: scenario 1, 2, 4; its findings also affect C-02 · Express REST API Server
Internet Attacker → C-02 · Express REST API Server: scenario 1, 3, 4, 5
Internet Attacker → C-05 · Web3 / Wallet / NFT Surface: scenario 2, 4
Internet Attacker → Juice Shop User: scenario 6, 7
Dynamic code evaluation — evidence: routes/captcha.ts:22, routes/userProfile.ts:61
Further capabilities: XML parsing — evidence: lib/xml.ts:33; Server-side templates — evidence: server.ts:164
C-02 · Express REST API Server: External Service Credentials
C-03 · Authentication and Session Service: JWT Signing Key Material
C-05 · Web3 / Wallet / NFT Surface: External Service Credentials
C-06 · SQLite Persistent Datastore: User Account Credentials
C-06 · SQLite Persistent Datastore: User Personal Data
C-06 · SQLite Persistent Datastore: Order and Payment Records
C-06 · SQLite Persistent Datastore: Product Inventory
C-06 · SQLite Persistent Datastore: User Reviews and Feedback Content
C-07 · MarsDB Embedded In-Memory Store: Order and Payment Records
C-07 · MarsDB Embedded In-Memory Store: User Reviews and Feedback Content
Human user interacting with Juice Shop via a web browser. Registers, shops, solves challenges, and may hold admin or customer role.
g.text: Juice Shop via a web browser.

g.title: Google accounts.google.com OAuth 2.0 implicit flow endpoint. Browser-only integration: the Angular SPA redirects the user to Google and receives an access_token in the redirect URI fragment.
Ollama-compatible LLM inference endpoint (configurable via application.chatBot.llmApiUrl). Receives streamed chat prompts from the Express backend for the AI chatbot challenge.
Alchemy WebSocket RPC endpoint for Ethereum Sepolia testnet. Used by the NFT minting challenge to subscribe to on-chain NFTMinted events and verify wallet addresses.
Application role with elevated rights, evidenced by its access check.

Google OAuth Authorization Server df-013: Browser redirect to Google OAuth 2.0 implicit authorization endpoint with client_id and redirect_uri (HTTPS); OAuth 2.0 implicit flow to Google accounts.google.com; client_id in authorization request, no PKCE, no state parameter df-014: Google OAuth callback redirect to angular-spa with access_token in URL fragment (HTTPS); redirect callback carries access_token in fragment; no state parameter to verify CSRF (missing oauth-missing-state) df-017: OAuth profile request (HTTPS); The provider checks the OAuth access token sent with the request

C-01 · Angular SPA Frontend df-013: Browser redirect to Google OAuth 2.0 implicit authorization endpoint with client_id and redirect_uri (HTTPS); OAuth 2.0 implicit flow to Google accounts.google.com; client_id in authorization request, no PKCE, no state parameter df-014: Google OAuth callback redirect to angular-spa with access_token in URL fragment (HTTPS); redirect callback carries access_token in fragment; no state parameter to verify CSRF (missing oauth-missing-state) df-017: OAuth profile request (HTTPS); The provider checks the OAuth access token sent with the request

g.text: data flow · classification colour · two heads = bidirectional
trust boundary crossed between these columns
dashed outline = zone, not itself a boundary
solid = direct attack · dashed = via user
STRIDE-per-element: filled = threats found in that class
All Critical · High fills to 5 · +N = omitted High categories
counts on a node = threats per severity · ①–⑨ = attack scenario
badges also count scenarios that hit an asset stored there
Dynamic code evaluation = runs runtime data as program code
LLM + tools = model calls with executable application tools
Most security-critical functions always shown (at most 5), others up
to 3 labels per element: most critical first, then most severe linked
finding; +N = further labels, listed under Further capabilities.
Functions may go undetected: a missing label does not mean absence.
Matching E-labels indicate a connection; lines omitted.
